prompt:
A wide background illustration for the battle screen of a mythology card game, made by hand like a 1993 fantasy trading-card or game-book illustration: bold, wobbly black pen-and-ink outlines around every shape, filled with thin, flat, transparent watercolour and gouache washes. Big simple flat shapes of colour with almost no shading or modelling, a little ink cross-hatching in the shadows, blotchy uneven washes with hard dried edges, splatters and visible brush marks, and the rough off-white paper texture and grain clearly showing through the paint. Naive, slightly clumsy, decorative and stylised, like an old printed card with slightly faded, misregistered colour. A limited palette of 4 or 5 colours, dark overall. Absolutely not realistic: no realistic lighting, no glow, no soft gradients, no depth of field, no fine detail or texture rendering, no oil-painting look, no 3D, no digital painting, not modern concept art. Composition for a game board: low contrast, all the interesting shapes at the edges and in the bottom corners; the centre is a calm, empty, evenly dark area, because game cards sit on top of it. No figures or creatures in the centre. No text, no letters, no border, no frame, no logo, no signature.

Setting: the island of Aeaea from Homer's Odyssey: the stone hall of the witch Circe in a dark forest clearing; tall oaks along the left and right edges; her great loom and a bronze mixing bowl with a steaming potion at the far left; tame wolves and mountain lions lying as dark shapes along the right edge, and a few pigs in a sty at the lower right; smoke rising from her hearth; violet dusk sky through the trees.
Colour: near-black plum to deep violet (#160d1c to #7a4a8a) with a few glowing magenta and pale gold accents.
